intro.title: focus-visible and a11y
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple navigation menu with buttons and links to learn how to improve accessibility for keyboard users. You will use the CSS `:focus-visible` pseudo-class to create clear, visible focus indicators that only appear when needed, such as when navigating with a keyboard. This involves writing CSS rules to style focus states without affecting mouse or touch interactions. By the end, you'll understand how `:focus-visible` helps make web interfaces more accessible (a11y) and user-friendly for everyone.
intro.usecase: The :focus-visible pseudo-class is essential for building accessible interactive components in modern web applications. Developers use it to provide clear visual focus indicators for keyboard users in complex UIs like data dashboards with interactive charts, multi-step forms with tabbed navigation, and application toolbars with button groups. This ensures that users navigating with a keyboard or assistive technology can always see where they are on the page, which is a critical requirement for compliance with accessibility standards (WCAG). Implementing :focus-visible correctly prevents focus rings from appearing unnecessarily during mouse interactions, maintaining a clean visual design while upholding core accessibility principles.
